title: Before Adam
summary: A modern young man suffers since childhood from vivid, terrifying dreams unlike any waking experience—endless primeval forests, predatory beasts, and a haunting sense of kinship with a lost world. Drawing on evolutionary theory learned in college, he concludes these are not fantasies but inherited race-memories, transmitted through the germplasm from a distant ancestor whose life he relives nightly with unusual completeness. The bulk of the narrative is that ancestor's story: a Mid-Pleistocene boy nicknamed Big-Tooth, one of the primitive, half-human "Tree People" or Folk, who are more advanced than apes but far short of true humanity. Big-Tooth recounts his upbringing among the horde, his friendship with the loyal Lop-Ear, his infatuation with the Swift One, and the horde's ongoing terror of the brutal, dominant Red-Eye, an atavistic throwback even among his own kind. Woven through are encounters with rival hominid groups—the fire-wielding, more advanced Fire People and the ape-like Tree People—along with constant struggles against predators, flood, and migration. The novel closes with Big-Tooth's family founding a new home, from which line the narrator's racial memories ultimately descend, blending speculative anthropology with an adventure tale of prehistoric survival.
